name: Strait of Malacca Route
insurance_premium: Standard rates; no elevated war risk premium
controller: Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia — littoral states. US Navy patrols. China increasingly assertive via South China Sea proximity
strategic_value: World's busiest chokepoint — connects Pacific to Indian Ocean. China's 'Malacca Dilemma' drives BRI port investments and pipeline alternatives through Myanmar
alert: Any closure would strand 25% of global trade. China has no naval capacity to secure it unilaterally

name: Suez Canal Route
traffic_volume: ~20,000 vessels/year pre-2023 — dropped to ~9,000 effective transit rate post-Houthi attacks. 12% of global trade
trade_value: $1 trillion annually (pre-disruption); Egypt lost ~60% of canal revenue by mid-2024
insurance_premium: War risk premium surged from 0.07% to 0.5-1.0% of hull value post-Nov 2023. Some insurers refusing Red Sea coverage entirely
controller: Egypt (Suez Canal Authority) — but Houthi attacks on Red Sea approach have made transit untenable for most commercial shipping since Nov 2023
strategic_value: Europe-Asia shortcut saving 10-14 days vs Cape route. Critical for IMEC corridor viability. Egypt's $9B/yr revenue stream
alert: Houthi attacks since Nov 2023 forced 60%+ of traffic to reroute around Cape of Good Hope. IMEC corridor viability in question

name: Cape of Good Hope Diversion Route
traffic_volume: Surged 40%+ since late 2023 — absorbing rerouted Suez traffic. ~6,000+ additional transits/year
trade_value: Handling $400B+ in rerouted cargo annually. Adds $1M+ per voyage in fuel costs
insurance_premium: Standard rates — safe but expensive due to distance. No war risk premium
controller: South Africa (Cape Town/Durban ports). Open ocean — no chokepoint controller. UK/US naval presence at Ascension and Diego Garcia
strategic_value: Fallback route when Red Sea/Suez is denied. Adds 10-14 days and $1M+ per voyage. Now the de facto Europe-Asia route for most carriers
tag: THE LONG WAY ROUND — NOW DEFAULT
alert: 40%+ surge in traffic since 2024. Supply chain delays rippling globally. Some carriers permanently shifting schedules

name: Strait of Hormuz Route
traffic_volume: ~138 vessels/day, 20% of global oil — 21 million barrels/day
trade_value: $1.2 trillion in oil annually at current prices
insurance_premium: War risk premium at historic highs — 5-10% of hull value after Feb 2026 closure. Most insurers pulled coverage
controller: Iran controls northern shore and has closed the strait as of Feb 2026. US Fifth Fleet based in Bahrain. UAE/Oman on southern shore
strategic_value: World's most critical oil chokepoint. Closure triggers immediate global energy crisis. Iran's ultimate leverage card
alert: CLOSED: Iran shut the strait Feb 28, 2026. All corridors threatened. Global oil prices spiking

name: Panama Canal Route
traffic_volume: ~14,000 transits/year normal — dropped to ~8,500 during 2023-2024 drought. 6% of global trade
insurance_premium: No war risk — but drought surcharges and slot auction premiums reached $4M per transit in late 2023
controller: Panama Canal Authority. China (HKND/CK Hutchison) operates ports at both canal ends — Balboa and Cristobal. US retains defense treaty rights
strategic_value: Americas trade spine. Climate vulnerability exposed in 2023. China's port operations at both ends raise strategic concerns
alert: 2023-2024 drought cut capacity 36%. CK Hutchison port deal flagged by US as national security risk

name: South China Sea Lanes
traffic_volume: 30% of global maritime trade — over $5 trillion in ship-borne trade annually
trade_value: $3.4 trillion in annual trade transiting the sea (partially overlaps with Malacca Strait figures)
insurance_premium: Standard rates but rising. Some underwriters adding 'China conflict' exclusion clauses since 2024
controller: China claims 90% via nine-dash line. Contested by Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, Taiwan. US Navy conducts freedom of navigation ops
strategic_value: Nexus of Asia-Pacific trade. China's artificial islands create de facto military control. Any conflict over Taiwan would close these lanes
alert: China has 7 militarized artificial islands. Any Taiwan scenario closes $5T in annual trade

name: Baltic Sea / Danish Straits Route
traffic_volume: ~70,000 vessels/year. Major Russian oil/gas and grain export route
trade_value: $350 billion annually — primarily energy and commodities
insurance_premium: Elevated since 2022 — war risk premiums for Russian-flagged vessels. NATO surveillance intensive
controller: NATO (Denmark controls straits). Russia maintains Baltic Fleet at Kaliningrad and St. Petersburg. Undersea infrastructure (Nord Stream) sabotaged 2022
strategic_value: Russia's western maritime trade outlet. Nord Stream sabotage (Sep 2022) severed gas link. NATO essentially controls access
alert: Nord Stream sabotaged Sep 2022. Russia's Baltic trade under NATO surveillance. Undersea cable sabotage incidents 2023-2024

name: Bab al-Mandab / Red Sea Route
traffic_volume: ~25,000 transits/year pre-2023 — dropped 70%+ since Houthi campaign began Nov 2023
trade_value: $200 billion in rerouted cargo costs since Nov 2023
insurance_premium: War risk premium 1-2% of hull value — up from near zero. Many insurers refusing Red Sea coverage. Additional $500K-$2M per transit
controller: Houthi forces (Yemen) — Iranian-backed. Control eastern shore of Bab al-Mandab. Djibouti/Eritrea on western shore. US/France/China have bases in Djibouti
strategic_value: Southern gateway to Suez Canal. Houthi campaign is the most effective non-state trade disruption in modern history. Iran's proxy leverage
alert: ACTIVE COMBAT ZONE: 100+ Houthi attacks since Nov 2023. Most commercial shipping rerouted to Cape. US/UK strikes have not stopped attacks

name: Trans-Pacific Route (US-China)
traffic_volume: Largest bilateral trade route by container volume — ~26 million TEU/year
trade_value: $575 billion annually (US-China bilateral, 2024). Down from $690B peak in 2022 due to tariffs and decoupling
insurance_premium: Standard maritime rates. Political risk — tariff escalation and potential sanctions — is the primary cost driver
controller: Open ocean — no chokepoint. US Navy dominates Pacific. China building blue-water capability. Trade disrupted by tariffs not kinetic action
strategic_value: Economic backbone of US-China relationship. Tariff wars and decoupling reducing volumes. Nearshoring to Mexico/Vietnam accelerating
alert: Trade volumes declining as US-China decoupling accelerates. 2025-2026 tariff escalation hitting all sectors

name: Trans-Atlantic Route (US-EU)
traffic_volume: ~5 million TEU/year container traffic plus massive bulk/tanker flows
trade_value: $1.1 trillion in annual bilateral goods trade (US-EU)
insurance_premium: Standard rates. Lowest risk major trade route
controller: NATO naval dominance. US and European navies. No contested chokepoints on route
strategic_value: Most secure major trade route. Allied naval control throughout. Foundation of Western economic bloc

name: Indian Ocean Crossing (India-ME-Africa Triangle)
traffic_volume: ~50,000 vessel transits/year across the Indian Ocean basin
insurance_premium: Elevated in western Indian Ocean due to Houthi spillover. Eastern basin standard rates
controller: India (dominant regional navy). China expanding presence via String of Pearls (Gwadar, Hambantota, Djibouti). US at Diego Garcia. France at Reunion
strategic_value: INSTC corridor spine. India-Middle East energy lifeline. China's String of Pearls encirclement strategy targets this zone
tag: STRING OF PEARLS VS INDIAN NAVY
alert: China operates ports at Gwadar (Pakistan), Hambantota (Sri Lanka), and Djibouti base — encircling India's home waters

name: Arctic Northern Sea Route
traffic_volume: ~90 transits in 2023 — up from near zero a decade ago. Still seasonal (Jul-Nov). Russia targets 150M tons cargo by 2030
trade_value: $2 billion in cargo (2023) — minuscule but growing. LNG from Yamal is primary cargo
insurance_premium: Very high — ice risk, lack of SAR infrastructure, Russia-only icebreaker support. 3-5x standard rates
controller: Russia (claims full jurisdiction). Requires Russian icebreaker escort. China declared itself 'near-Arctic state' in 2018. Western sanctions limit investment
strategic_value: Climate change opening new route 30% shorter than Suez for Asia-Europe. Russia-China strategic corridor. Western sanctions blocking development
alert: Russia investing $30B+ in Arctic infrastructure. China building icebreakers. Route viability accelerating with climate change

name: East Africa Coastal Route
traffic_volume: ~15,000 vessel transits/year along East African coast
trade_value: $120 billion — connecting Horn of Africa ports to Southern Africa and Indian Ocean
insurance_premium: Elevated — Somali piracy legacy plus Houthi spillover. War risk surcharges south of Bab al-Mandab
controller: Fragmented — Djibouti hosts US, China, France, Japan bases. Somalia unstable. Kenya, Tanzania expanding port capacity with Chinese investment
strategic_value: BRI anchor — China has invested $50B+ in East African ports and rail. Djibouti base is China's first overseas military facility. Horn of Africa is proxy battlefield
alert: China's Djibouti base 10km from US Camp Lemonnier. Lamu Port (Kenya) — China-funded. Bagamoyo (Tanzania) — stalled Chinese mega-port

name: Mediterranean East-West Lane
insurance_premium: Standard rates. Eastern Med slightly elevated due to regional conflicts
controller: NATO navies dominate. Turkey controls Bosphorus access to Black Sea. COSCO/China operates Piraeus (Greece) — key BRI transshipment hub
strategic_value: IMEC terminal segment. BRI enters Europe via Piraeus. Suez Canal feeds eastern entrance. Critical for Europe's supply chains
alert: COSCO controls 67% of Piraeus — Greece's largest port and BRI gateway into Europe. Turkey leverages Bosphorus as strategic card
